primitives.name: Git repository availability verification
primitives.verbatim_quote: Other plausible clones were found, but this one was selected as the active app clone for evidence because it is the known primary shipping clone and contains the runnable app.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes deterministic git history, identical remote origins, and functional node_modules in the selected clone.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs when the selected clone's HEAD diverges from the remote origin, breaking verifiability.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's probabilistic model of source authenticity, where git hash verification serves as empirical telemetry for Bayesian posterior updates on code provenance.
layer2.telemetry: Git object hashes (blobs/tree/commit), remote tracking branches, and node_module directory presence serve as observables.

primitives.name: Branch consistency verification
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Git root: C:/Users/Garrett/Sports - Branch: safety/sports-wip-2026-06-04 - Remote: https://github.com/BeeXly/Sports.git - HEAD observed: f897fd5 wip(sports): safety
primitives.assumptions: Assumes a linear git workflow without rebasing, and that the 'safety' prefix indicates a protected feature branch.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Regime failure occurs when the branch is force-pushed, corrupting the historical HEAD link.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's state-transition logic, where branch checkout triggers a specific configuration state (e.g., feature flag set) and initiates a localized reasoning loop.
layer2.telemetry: Git reflog entries, working tree status, and npm script execution context serve as verification metrics.

primitives.name: Node module dependency resolution
primitives.verbatim_quote: cockpit/journal updates + brand/emails/social packages - Dirty state observed: 62 entries - Package manager: npm through
primitives.assumptions: Assumes a monorepo structure with deterministic npm install behavior under specified Node version.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breakdown occurs when npm dependencies conflict or when the Node version mismatch causes runtime errors.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's conformal inference framework, where resolved dependencies form a high-dimensional feature vector used to calibrate predictive intervals for software composition analysis.
layer2.telemetry: package-lock.json file size, installed package versions, and npm audit results serve as empirical observables.

primitives.name: Git repository integrity verification
primitives.verbatim_quote: Windows PowerShell - Node observed: v24.15.0 - Root package: sports-prediction-platform - Web package: @sports/web ## Why
primitives.assumptions: Assumes that the presence of the full app tree, manifests, and node_modules guarantees functional equivalence to the shipped artifact.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure mode arises when the local node_modules are corrupted or missing essential binaries, preventing the app from running.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's situational reasoning via a verification automaton that transitions between 'clean', 'dirty', and 'corrupted' states based on git status codes and npm install exit codes.
layer2.telemetry: Git status return codes, npm install success/failure, and file existence checks (e.g., package.json) provide state-transition triggers.
